data_sources.fallback_if_unavailable: Use a fresh independently documented official play-by-play provider only with recorded provenance and field/timing harmonization. Source descriptions flag games without play coverage; do not manufacture decisions from schedules. If recovery is unavailable, retain a coverage limitation and let the sealed branch evaluate sample accounting.

data_sources.fallback_if_unavailable: Use the described byte/content-equivalent nfldata games copy with provenance. Do not replace in-game performance with a closing betting spread or final score.

unit_of_observation: An offensive-team decision on fourth down within a regular-season game, after regulation/time restrictions (D01 PDF p. 8, Data and Risk Taking; PDF pp. 15–16, Endnotes 1–3).

sample_steps.rule: Load the S1 season files for seasons 2000 through 2005 inclusive. Keep season_type == REG; use season, not calendar year. For game summaries use the S2 regular-season game universe for the same seasons. Audit unavailable game coverage without fabricating play rows. Source mapping: data_description/source_descriptions.md, S1–S2.

Verify S1 keys game_id + play_id and S2 game_id uniqueness; merge S2 many-to-one by game_id. Resolve conflicting duplicate keys as a source-quality question rather than arbitrary deletion. Normalize team identities LA→STL, LAC→SD, LV→OAK for comparison with S2, retaining stable franchise identities for team effects. Source mapping: data_description/data_dictionary.md, Linkage.

sample_steps.rule: Retain regulation qtr in {1,2,3,4}; exclude all overtime. Do not exclude regulation plays merely because their game later enters overtime.

Start from down == 4. Remove administrative events (timeouts and period-end markers), kickoff/extra-point/two-point events, and deleted plays when documented by the source. Closest executable convention: retain actual pass/run/punt/field-goal plays with a known offensive team; distinguish an executed play with a penalty from an administrative no_play row. Classification of nullified plays, kneels, spikes, fakes, aborted kicks, and intentional safeties is not specified; flag them for a prespecified adjudication rule, leaving unknown decisions missing. Do not define the outcome from conversion success alone or silently classify every non-kick row as an attempt.

source.where: Data; Risk Taking; appendix on PDF p. 15

sample_steps.rule: Remove plays with regulation game_seconds_remaining <= 120. This implements removal of the last two minutes; the exact treatment of a snap at 02:00 is not explicit. Keep the end of the first half. Prefer the pre-play clock, and flag disagreements with (4-qtr)*900 + quarter_seconds_remaining.

Construct all variables below from the pre-play state. Obtain a documented season-specific conference-membership lookup before deriving same_conference. S2.div_game supplies same_division. Do not replace either explicit control with a proxy, omit it, or infer its coding from a desired numerical result.

The publication does not state a missing-data rule. Proposed origin: use a common complete-case set on the union of M1–M3 variables after sample and classification rules are settled, record exclusions, and use no imputation or weights. Report any groups lost through conditional likelihood or separation. This is an implementation assumption requiring freezing before fitting, not a documented exclusion.

variables.name: risk_taking
variables.definition: Offensive choice on fourth down: conversion attempt versus punt or field-goal attempt, regardless of success. For unambiguous executed S1 pass/run (including sacks and scrambles) classify as attempt, and for unambiguous punt/field_goal classify as non-attempt. Use description and kick flags to detect conflicts/fakes; unresolved unusual plays remain missing until a coding rule is frozen.
variables.coding: 1 = conversion attempted; 0 = punt or field goal attempted; missing is not 0

variables.name: performance_gap
variables.definition: Auxiliary pre-play point gap relative to aspiration: d = posteam_score - (defteam_score + 1) = score_differential - 1. Subtract the aspiration offset once, not twice. Use the worked example in the methods to disambiguate wording. Provider pre-play score columns are preferred over total_home_score/total_away_score, whose timing is disputed in the supplied dictionary.
variables.coding: points; d = 0 means offense leads by one; a tied score gives d = -1

variables.name: performance_below
variables.definition: b = min(d,0), with missing d remaining missing; negative distance below the aspiration threshold, zero above.
variables.coding: continuous signed points, no absolute value or standardization

variables.name: performance_below_sq
variables.definition: b*b, where b is performance_below; zero above aspiration, missing if b missing.
variables.coding: squared points, not square of the unsplit gap for all observations

variables.name: performance_above
variables.definition: a = max(d,0), with missing d remaining missing; positive distance above aspiration, zero at or below.
variables.coding: continuous points

variables.name: below_indicator
variables.definition: Indicator for d <= 0. Allows different intercepts on either side of the aspiration threshold. Equality belongs to the below branch. Table 5 includes this in M2 and M3; general prose says each model, creating an unresolved inconsistency for M1.
variables.coding: 1 for d <= 0; 0 for d > 0; unknown d stays missing

source.where: Performance / indicator; Table 5 on PDF p. 11

variables.name: minutes_remaining
variables.definition: t = game_seconds_remaining/60 before the play, preserving seconds as fractions of a minute. Cross-check against ((4-qtr)*900 + quarter_seconds_remaining)/60. Larger t means a more distant deadline. The article does not state integer rounding or centering.
variables.coding: continuous uncentered minutes; inferred exact seconds conversion

variables.name: below_x_time
variables.definition: performance_below * minutes_remaining. Construct from the same underlying gap and clock; propagate missingness.
variables.coding: ordinary product; no centering described

variables.name: below_sq_x_time
variables.definition: performance_below_sq * minutes_remaining. Construct from the same underlying gap and clock; propagate missingness.
variables.coding: ordinary product; no centering described

variables.name: above_x_time
variables.definition: performance_above * minutes_remaining. Construct from the same underlying gap and clock; propagate missingness.
variables.coding: ordinary product; no centering described

variables.name: total_points
variables.definition: Offensive-team points already accumulated before the play; use posteam_score, not final home_score/away_score or post-play scores.
variables.coding: continuous points

variables.name: yards_first_down
variables.definition: Pre-play yards needed to gain a first down, or to reach the end zone in goal-to-go situations; use S1.ydstogo. Goal-to-go handling is source-based inference.
variables.coding: continuous yards

variables.name: yards_touchdown
variables.definition: Distance from the pre-play line of scrimmage to the opponent end zone; use yardline_100, not yards from own end zone or kick_distance.
variables.coding: continuous yards

variables.name: same_division
variables.definition: Same-division opponent indicator from S2.div_game, joined by game_id. Natural affirmative coding is inferred because the article does not give binary codes; do not invert or exchange labels without clarification.
variables.coding: proposed 1 = same division, 0 = different division; retain missing

variables.name: same_conference
variables.definition: Join offense and defense to a season-specific franchise-to-conference crosswalk and compare membership. Same division is ordinarily nested within same conference. Crosswalk is absent from supplied source descriptions; include realignment and franchise-entry timing only from documented information. A same-conference-excluding-division indicator is not explicitly stated.
variables.coding: proposed 1 = same conference (including same division), 0 = different conference; unavailable membership stays missing

variables.name: home_field
variables.definition: Whether offense plays in its own stadium. Proposed origin uses S1.posteam_type == home for ordinary home venues and checks S2.location for neutral venues. A designated home team at a neutral or relocated venue is not necessarily at home; those cases need a documented rule.
variables.coding: 1 = home-field advantage, 0 = away; neutral/relocated cases unresolved

variables.name: season_week
variables.definition: Numbered week within the regular season, not team games played; use S1.week and cross-check S2.week.
variables.coding: continuous ordinal week; no week fixed effects specified

variables.name: offense_team
variables.definition: Offensive franchise identity, normalized consistently across files and seasons. Closest reading is conditional-logit panel identifier by offensive franchise, not game, team-game, or team-season; exact panel declaration is absent.
variables.coding: categorical franchise; no opponent fixed effect stated

variables.name: season_effect
variables.definition: Season indicators, with a reference season omitted. Season is the football season, including games played in the following calendar year. Separate season effects rather than team-by-season effects are the closest reading.
variables.coding: categorical; reference choice does not change fitted index when transformed consistently

variables.name: quarters_remaining
variables.definition: For the narrative robustness check, replace remaining minutes with an ordinal measure based on qtr. Candidate definition is 5-qtr, including the current quarter. Whether the article instead used 4-qtr, fractional quarters, or rounding is unstated. A constant shift is equivalent only if all associated main terms are retained and transformed consistently.
variables.coding: robustness template only; do not add alongside minutes_remaining in the primary models

variables.name: recent_spread_aspiration
variables.definition: Narrative robustness alternative using a recently held point spread as aspiration. Lookback, reset rules, statistic and lag are absent; construction must remain undefined until documentary clarification.
variables.coding: not executable from publication; no assumed rolling window

variables.name: within_field_goal_range
variables.definition: Sample selector only for narrative robustness models; field-goal range cutoff and treatment of punts inside or kicks outside are not given. Requires a preregistered, documented rule; do not substitute nflverse expected-points or win-probability models.
variables.coding: not a primary-model regressor; binary restriction currently undefined

models.link: logit; risk_taking=1 is the modeled event
models.covariance: not stated; conventional information-matrix covariance is an inferred origin, not a reported fact
models.software_defaults_relevant: Specify fixed-effects estimation explicitly; do not rely on an unstated xtlogit default. Record likelihood type, optimizer, convergence tolerances, reference season, covariance and treatment of outcome-constant groups. No weights are described. Standard-error transformation for displayed odds ratios is unspecified. No game or team clustering is explicitly stated.
models.missing_data_rule: Not stated. Proposed common complete-case sample on the union of primary model variables; unresolved classifications remain missing. Do not impute values or alter controls to recover a target. Any alternative modelwise deletion needs an explicit recorded branch.
models.post_estimation: Report exp(beta), coefficient- and odds-ratio-scale SEs with their scale labeled, log likelihood, model test and model degrees of freedom. This is the controls-only origin from Table 5; an indicator is not listed here despite general methods wording.

models.post_estimation: Report exp(beta), coefficient- and odds-ratio-scale SEs with their scale labeled, log likelihood, model test and model degrees of freedom. Compare to the preceding nested model using the same observations and likelihood; state the null constraints. Compute performance derivatives on the probability scale at d = -42,-28,-14,0,14,28,42. For d < 0, slope of the logit index is beta_b + 2*d*beta_b2; for d > 0 it is beta_a. Evaluate remaining time and controls at sample means as a documented inference; the article only explicitly states mean controls for the figures. At d=0 use a labeled left derivative because a jump makes a two-sided derivative undefined. Probability levels require an explicit fixed-effect prediction rule: conditional estimation does not itself supply a unique intercept/individual-effect prediction. Means/reference levels of season and team effects, confidence intervals and marginal-effect covariance method are not specified. Preserve these as unresolved; delta-method SEs using the full covariance are a proposed inference rule. Compute the local derivative multiplied by seven separately from the exact probability change after seven points; do not equate these. A true touchdown scenario also changes total_points, whereas the partial performance derivative holds it fixed.

inference.observation_unit: Fourth-down offensive decision (D01 PDF p. 8, Risk Taking).
inference.sampling_unit: Regular-season game coverage, with repeated plays nested within games and franchises across seasons; no probability-sampling design described (D01 PDF p. 8, Data).
inference.assignment_unit_of_focal_variables: Observed offensive-team game state at each decision; no randomized treatment assignment, instrument, or first stage (D01 PDF p. 9, Performance and Deadline Proximity).
inference.clusters: No cluster variable stated. Team fixed effects address level heterogeneity, but do not establish cluster-robust inference (D01 PDF p. 9, Data Analysis Model).
inference.native_se_method: Standard errors printed; covariance estimator and marginal-effect SE method not stated. Conventional model-based covariance is only a proposed origin (D01 PDF p. 11, Table 5 note; PDF p. 12, Table 6).
inference.test_tail_and_direction: Tail not stated. Below-aspiration shape requires slopes of different signs across the gap; above-aspiration hypothesis is positive. Moderation is defined as remaining time decreases. Do not convert directional hypotheses into one-tailed tests without a declared assumption (D01 PDF pp. 4,7,11–12).
inference.alpha: Significance legend uses thresholds 0.10, 0.05 and 0.01; no unique primary threshold or multiplicity adjustment stated (D01 PDF p. 11, Table 5 note; PDF p. 12, Table 6 note).

open_questions: S1 and S2 are independent later-vintage sources. The original play provider, download date, game-level exclusions and parser are not specified (D01 PDF p. 8, Data; data_description/source_descriptions.md, S1–S2). Which documentary source can resolve coverage and the original play universe?

Does a play at exactly 02:00 belong to the excluded terminal interval? What is the protocol for nullified plays, repeated downs, fakes, aborted kicks, kneels, spikes and deliberate safeties? Primary sample and outcome descriptions do not specify these (D01 PDF p. 8, Risk Taking; PDF pp. 15–16, Endnote 3).

Supply season-specific conference membership and clarify affirmative versus reverse coding of same_division and same_conference, inclusive versus exclusive conference membership, and neutral/relocated home venues. Preserve the explicit control list (D01 PDF p. 9, Control Variables).

Which panel identifier and xtlogit options were used? Were team effects conditioned out or explicitly estimated? Were season effects separate or interacted with teams? Which covariance and software version? Do not introduce clustering as a claimed native method (D01 PDF p. 9, Data Analysis Model).

Methods state the threshold indicator enters each model, but Table 5 has no indicator in Model 1. The listed origin follows the table and retains this contradiction; clarify before executing an alternative (D01 PDF p. 9, Performance; PDF p. 11, Table 5).

What missing-data and separation rules were used? Does each model use its own complete cases or the common union? The proposed common sample is not stated as such (D01 PDF p. 9, Data Analysis Model; PDF p. 11, Table 5).

How were intercepts, team effects and year effects handled when predicting probabilities after fixed-effects estimation? Which values of other regressors were used for Table 6, and which delta-method or other covariance formula was used? Is the zero-gap effect a one-sided derivative or discrete change? (D01 PDF pp. 11–13, Results, Table 6 and Figures 2–3.)

Narrative robustness family RQ: repeat the analysis replacing t with quarters_remaining and regenerate each performance interaction. The number of repeated models and ordinal coding are not given; the natural template mirrors M1–M3 but must not be represented as exactly reported. Keep all controls and fixed effects. No numerical robustness output is available (D01 PDF p. 9, Deadline Proximity).

Narrative robustness family RA: recent_spread_aspiration would replace the aspiration reference and require rebuilding both spline pieces, the squared piece, jump and interactions. Lookback and reset rules are missing, and the exact models repeated are unknown. Obtain prose/tables rather than author code (D01 PDF p. 16, Endnote 4).

Narrative robustness families RF and RP: estimate conversion versus field goal within field-goal range and conversion versus punt outside range, preserving the primary controls unless new documentary material specifies otherwise. Cutoff, treatment of the third choice, formula and repeated model set are unavailable; these are distinct restricted estimands, not interchangeable specifications (D01 PDF p. 16, Endnote 4).

The below/above aspiration comparison test does not specify its restrictions; do not silently substitute either the jump test or the joint addition-of-performance-terms test (D01 PDF p. 10, Results, final paragraph).
